source_of_truth: Published 0.85.0 registry archive. Its dirty VCS marker means the recorded revision is not an identical source substitute. Original Cargo.lock is recorded but omitted; workspace Cargo.lock controls resolution.
local_changes: Timestamp::unpack_native admits every Int64 storage value for timezone-free microseconds. TimestampValue::fmt uses checked direct calendar conversion for that case and exact epoch-microsecond display outside the calendar. Other units and timezone policy are unchanged. StatsSet count/size merging uses checked u64 addition, invalidating overflow without host-pointer-width dependence. src/array adds an optional opaque metadata owner retained after encoding data through construction parts, clones and structural rewrites; attachment requires a unique previously unowned array. Buffer reconstruction preserves a provider-supplied owner and rejects conflicts. Owned slices and filters retain a native parent view until execution while ownerless arrays keep existing optimization. src/arrays/slice/vtable.rs reduces that view at explicit execution to prevent repeated slice reconstruction over an already canonical child. src/arrays/filter/vtable.rs applies deferred filter reductions at execution while retaining the original array through canonical execution. No unsafe code or serialized field is added. src/array/owner_tests.rs is original ShardLoom lifetime, execution and common-allocation-footprint verification. A blank doc line in src/arrays/patched/mod.rs loses trailing whitespace; the snapshot in src/scalar_fn/fns/zip/mod.rs uses an ordinary string with an explicit space escape to preserve its original expected bytes without trailing whitespace. Every modified source file has a change notice. Cargo.toml is marked publish=false; license, provenance and README.shardloom.md are added. External heap admission is available through HostAllocator::reserve_external(len), which returns an opaque lifetime owner; covered provider allocations must be freed before the owner is dropped. Custom allocators refuse reservations by default, while DefaultHostAllocator explicitly remains unbounded.
